title: U-Mamba: Enhancing Long-range Dependency for Biomedical Image Segmentation
mechanism: Hybrid conv + Mamba (SSM) blocks in the encoder (U-Mamba Enc) or only the bottleneck (U-Mamba Bot), self-configured inside nnU-Net.
adaptation: Run U-Mamba Bot only, always with its No-Mamba control (same net, Mamba layers off), at 512 px 2D; the bottleneck is 16 x 16 tokens, so global mixing is cheap. Target the E1 context gap.
min_experiment: U-Mamba Bot against No-Mamba Base on 5 module-grouped folds; metric E1 crack relF1@2 and CV crack relF1@2. Kill: difference within fold SD.
evidence: R (original): beats CNN/Transformer baselines on abdomen CT/MR, endoscopy and microscopy. R (nnU-Net Revisited): the No-Mamba control matches U-Mamba on all 6 3D datasets, so the gains came from the residual U-Net.
prior_overlap: none here. Externally weakened by the Revisited ablation, which is why the No-Mamba control is required.

alt_notes.adaptation: Suite member: U-Mamba_Bot 2D at 512 px, same folds and label-safe aug; needs mamba-ssm CUDA kernels (install requires OK). Always paired with the No-Mamba ablation, as Revisited did.
alt_notes.min_experiment: U-Mamba_Bot v No-Mamba base, 5 folds each. Kill (for score purposes) if E1 relF1@2 difference < 0.03; keep as benchmark row regardless.
